methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: A regional initiative explicitly evaluating AI adoption in the Roanoke Valley signals grassroots capability-building outside traditional tech hubs, suggesting potential for distributed deep learning if sustained beyond evaluation phase.

signals.title: Virginia's AI challenge isn't data centers. It's small-business adoption | Guest column - Richmond Times-Dispatch
signals.signal_reading: This commentary explicitly identifies small-business adoption as Virginia's real AI challenge, signaling that infrastructure concentration (data centers) is not translating to distributed capability—a hallmark of shallow/concentrated outcomes.

signals.title: Virginia advanced manufacturing hub receives $24.8M federal grant
signals.signal_reading: Federal funding for advanced manufacturing hubs risks reinforcing concentrated expertise unless deliberately distributed across regions; the $24.8M investment likely flows to existing capability centers rather than building new ones in underserved areas.

signals.title: Sentara hospitals are using AI to help monitor patients, determine discharge timelines
signals.signal_reading: Sentara's platform-delivered AI for patient monitoring represents shallow but distributed adoption—healthcare systems implementing vendor solutions without building deep internal AI capability, extending reach but not depth.

signals.title: Mace AI funds AI safety research at University of Virginia’s School of Data Science (UVA) - TheStreet
signals.signal_reading: Private AI safety research funding at UVA's Data Science School deepens metro academic capability but concentrates cutting-edge expertise in established research institutions rather than distributing knowledge infrastructure regionally.
